course_name_original: LAB ON ELECTRONIC MEASUREMENTS FOR MEDICAL APPLICATIONS (86620)
course_name_en: LAB ON ELECTRONIC MEASUREMENTS FOR MEDICAL APPLICATIONS

learning_outcomes.text: Apply measurement methods to characterize biomedical Data Acquisition Systems (DAQ), evaluating key performance metrics (e.g., SNR, PSSR, uncertainty).
Perform calibration of DAQ systems and medical instruments against gold standard references, understanding the importance of these measurements for validating accuracy and regulatory compliance.
Design and numerically model biomedical measurement circuits for medical applications.
Apply Digital Signal Processing (DSP) techniques (e.g., FIR/IIR, adaptive filters) and machine learning to analyze calibrated biomedical signals.
Develop practical skills in simulation, circuit design, and calibration of smart measurement systems.
Analyze intelligent sensors and systems within the context of calibration and validation for medical applications.

syllabus_topics: Electronic Measurement Instrumentation for Biomedical Applications
Measurement methods and characterization techniques for DAQ systems: Measuring noise and distortion in biomedical DAQ
Evaluating bandwidth and sampling frequency
Calibration techniques to ensure accuracy (e.g., for ECG, EEG)
Transfer function: Experimental determination of the transfer function in an electronics lab (e.g., with a signal generator, oscilloscope, spectrum analyzer)
Theoretical modeling (e.g., frequency response of a sensor amplifier)
Applications: Characterization of DAQ systems for biomedical signals
Biocompatibility and safety (ISO 13485, IEC 60601, MDR standards)
Medical applications: Monitoring, telemedicine, diagnostics
Design of Data Acquisition Systems (DAQ) for Medical Applications
Low-power DAQ architecture: Design considerations for reduced power consumption: power management techniques (e.g., sleep mode, duty cycling)
Importance of low power supply noise: effects of noise on the accuracy of biomedical signals
Power supply figures of merit: Power Supply Rejection Ratio (PSSR): Definition, measurement, and impact on medical DAQ (e.g., reducing power supply interference)
Other parameters: ripple, voltage stability, energy efficiency
Characterization techniques: measuring PSSR with a spectrum analyzer, power supply noise testing
Measurements for communication protocols in medical DAQ systems: I2C: Low power, suitable for local sensors (e.g., temperature sensors)
SPI: High speed for multi-parameter DAQ (e.g., ECG, EEG)
Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE): Wireless connectivity for wearable devices
LoRa: Long-range communication for remote monitoring in telemedicine
Comparison: power consumption, latency, reliability
Measured data visualization interfaces: Designing dashboards (virtual instrumentation) for real-time monitoring
Tools: Python applications
Requirements: usability, real-time updates, compatibility with medical standards
Real-time monitoring and measurement systems: Requirements: low latency, high precision, safety
Examples: DAQ for multi-parameter monitoring, low-power wearable systems for telemedicine
Techniques: data buffering, edge processing to reduce transmission
Medical applications: Real-time monitoring
Low-power wearable devices for real-time monitoring
Remote systems

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory Activities (development of a simple application)

assessment_rules: The final grade is determined by a combination of Laboratory Activities (30%) and an Oral Exam (70%).
bibliography: Slides and lecture notes written by the instructor
Scientific articles and datasheets provided by the instructor
